description: Issue #947 (adversarial review PR #953 F2 update): _FrameworkController.Selector's Ids branch (the "already selected" chip display) used to set SearcherMode.Batch and listVM.ReplaceWhere = listVM.Ids.GetContainIdExpression(...) to restrict the query to the caller-supplied Ids. DoSearch()'s ReplaceWhere handling runs the resulting query through WhereReplaceModifier, which deletes EVERY Where node in GetSearchQuery() -- including row-level DataPrivilege applied via DPWhere -- before rebuilding the query with only the Ids restriction. Any authenticated caller could therefore supply a VM name, an arbitrary Ids list, and a _DONOT_USE_VFIELD, and receive rows outside their DataPrivilege grant. The original #947 fix routed Selector through a new PopulateSelectedEntities method; a #953 adversarial review found that unnecessary (BasePagedListVM.GetBatchQuery()'s already-fixed default branch reaches the same GetAuthorizedIdsQuery mechanism through the ordinary DoSearch() pipeline once ReplaceWhere is simply never set) and found the bypassed DoSearch() pipeline silently skipped GetSearchCommand()-backed ListVMs and Searcher.SortInfo -- PopulateSelectedEntities was removed from BasePagedListVM and IBasePagedListVM. This mutant reverts the single remaining _FrameworkController.cs call site back to the pre-#947 SearcherMode.Batch + ReplaceWhere pair (SearcherMode.Batch itself is untouched -- it is still set unconditionally, two lines above, by both the fixed and the mutated code -- only the listVM.SelectorValueField = _DONOT_USE_VFIELD; line, and the local Expression-building variables it replaced, are reverted), reproducing the #947 defect. SelectorDataPrivilegeTests947's Selector_... test seeds two Schools and one Major per School, restricts an admin caller's DataPrivilege grant to only the allowed School, then posts both Majors' ids to Selector in one request together with a Searcher.Remark value matching neither Major. With the mutant applied, DataPrivilege is stripped and BOTH majors come back, turning the negative assertion red; on the unmutated (fixed) tree only the allowed Major is returned.
target_symbol: _FrameworkController.Selector's Ids branch -- the `listVM.SelectorValueField = _DONOT_USE_VFIELD;` line (reverted, along with the local `para`/`pro` Expression-building variables and the `System.Linq.Expressions` using directive, to `listVM.ReplaceWhere = listVM.Ids.GetContainIdExpression(modelType, Expression.Parameter(modelType), pro);`)

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Api.Test.SelectorDataPri: #947: a DataPrivilege-restricted caller must not receive a row

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured verbatim against the committed baseline (stale demo.db under bin/ removed first; mutant patch applied via `git apply`, test run, then reverted via `git apply -R`, rebuilt against the #953-corrected tree after PopulateSelectedEntities was removed): Selector_DataPrivilegeRestrictedCaller_Ids_ExcludesUnauthorized_IncludesAuthorized_IgnoresSearchCriteria -- 'Assert.IsFalse failed. #947: a DataPrivilege-restricted caller must not receive a row (forbiddenMajor, belonging to a school outside their DataPrivilege grant) they named directly in the Ids they posted to Selector -- SearcherMode.Batch + ReplaceWhere used to delete the DataPrivilege Where node from GetSearchQuery() before rebuilding the query with only the Ids restriction.' -- both the allowed and the forbidden Major's ids came back, exactly reproducing the pre-#947 DataPrivilege bypass. Under the #953-corrected tree this mutant ALSO turns the GetExportExcel_... test red (both tests now reach GetBatchQuery()'s default branch, see the #953 review's own note in SelectorDataPrivilegeTests947.cs) -- red_test_filter below is scoped to Selector_... only, so dotnet test --filter for THIS mutant does not include GetExportExcel_... in the same invocation; mutant 953-getbatchquery-wherereplacemodifier-reintroduce is the one that isolates and proves the GetExportExcel path independently. Manual dotnet test run of the mutated tree: 1 failed (the test above); the mutated tree still builds cleanly (0 errors).
